/**
 * Force a fresh Modbus TCP connection before each polling cycle.
 *
 * WHY?
 * ----
 * The SM61IoT closes idle Modbus TCP connections after its configured
 * "Port closing time". With a polling interval of 60 seconds, the socket
 * may already have been closed by the gateway when the next poll starts.
 *
 * node-red-contrib-modbus can still think the old socket exists until it
 * tries to use it, resulting in:
 *
 *   "Modbus client socket not readable"
 *
 * Therefore we explicitly reconnect before performing the actual
 * Modbus read.
 *
 * IMPORTANT:
 * The Modbus Flex Connector and the Modbus Flex Getter must use the
 * SAME "Modbus Client" configuration node.
 */


/* SM61IoT network configuration */
const MODBUS_HOST = "10.40.22.122";
const MODBUS_PORT = 502;
const UNIT_ID = 255;


/**
 * Modbus Flex Connector expects its configuration in msg.payload.
 *
 * connectorType = TCP
 * tcpType       = DEFAULT because the SM61IoT provides native Modbus TCP.
 */
msg.payload = {

    connectorType: "TCP",

    tcpHost: MODBUS_HOST,

    tcpPort: MODBUS_PORT,

    tcpType: "DEFAULT",

    unitId: UNIT_ID,

    /**
     * How long to wait for an individual Modbus transaction.
     */
    clientTimeout: 3000,

    /**
     * Delay used by the client between commands.
     */
    commandDelay: 100,

    /**
     * Delay used for automatic reconnect attempts.
     */
    reconnectTimeout: 2000
};


/**
 * Remember when this poll cycle started.
 *
 * The timestamp can later be passed through the Modbus request
 * and used for all meter MQTT messages belonging to this cycle.
 */
msg.pollTimestamp = new Date().toISOString();


return msg;

name: Modbus Request to SM61-3
func:
/**
 * Build Modbus requests for all configured electricity meters.
 *
 * PURPOSE
 * -------
 * The SM61IoT exposes the meter values as consecutive Modbus registers.
 *
 * Each electricity meter contains:
 *
 *   12 Float32 values
 *   2 Modbus registers per Float32 value
 *
 * Therefore one meter normally occupies:
 *
 *   12 * 2 = 24 Modbus registers
 *
 *
 * WHY MULTIPLE REQUESTS?
 * ----------------------
 * Modbus FC03 allows a maximum of 125 registers per request.
 *
 * Therefore multiple meters may need to be split into several requests.
 *
 * The split is configured explicitly using BLOCK_SIZES.
 *
 *
 * EXAMPLES
 * --------
 *
 * 9 meters split as 4 + 5:
 *
 *   const BLOCK_SIZES = [4, 5];
 *
 * Results in:
 *
 *   Request 1 -> A1-A4
 *   Request 2 -> A5-A9
 *
 *
 * 9 meters split as 3 + 3 + 3:
 *
 *   const BLOCK_SIZES = [3, 3, 3];
 *
 *
 * 8 meters split as 3 + 5:
 *
 *   const BLOCK_SIZES = [3, 5];
 *
 *
 * 7 meters split as 3 + 4:
 *
 *   const BLOCK_SIZES = [3, 4];
 *
 *
 * IMPORTANT
 * ---------
 * The sum of BLOCK_SIZES must exactly match the number of meters
 * configured in METERS.
 */


/* =========================================================
 * Modbus configuration
 * ========================================================= */


/**
 * Modbus TCP Unit-ID / Slave-ID of the SM61IoT.
 */
const UNIT_ID = 255;


/**
 * Float byte order used by the meter values.
 *
 * The currently observed values indicate ABCD.
 */
const FLOAT_ORDER = "ABCD";


/**
 * Maximum number of registers allowed by FC03.
 *
 * According to the Modbus specification:
 *
 *   FC03 quantity = 1 ... 125 registers
 */
const MAX_REGISTERS_PER_REQUEST = 125;


/* =========================================================
 * Request block configuration
 * ========================================================= */


/**
 * Define how many meters should be read in each Modbus request.
 *
 * Current gateway:
 *
 *   9 meters
 *
 * Split:
 *
 *   Request 1 -> 4 meters
 *   Request 2 -> 4 meters
 *   Request 3 -> 1 meters
 *
 * Therefore:
 */
const BLOCK_SIZES = [4];


/*
 * Other valid examples:
 *
 * const BLOCK_SIZES = [3, 3, 3];
 *
 * const BLOCK_SIZES = [3, 4];
 *
 * const BLOCK_SIZES = [3, 5];
 *
 * const BLOCK_SIZES = [2, 2, 2, 3];
 */


/* =========================================================
 * Meter field layout
 * ========================================================= */


/**
 * Every field is one Float32 value.
 *
 * One Float32 occupies two consecutive 16-bit Modbus registers.
 *
 * The offset is relative to the first register of the meter.
 */
const FIELDS = [

    { name: "u_l1_n", offset: 0 },
    { name: "u_l2_n", offset: 2 },
    { name: "u_l3_n", offset: 4 },

    { name: "i_l1", offset: 6 },
    { name: "i_l2", offset: 8 },
    { name: "i_l3", offset: 10 },

    { name: "p_l1", offset: 12 },
    { name: "p_l2", offset: 14 },
    { name: "p_l3", offset: 16 },

    { name: "p_sum", offset: 18 },

    { name: "energy_con", offset: 20 },
    { name: "energy_del", offset: 22 }

];


/* =========================================================
 * Meter / register relationship
 * ========================================================= */


/**
 * Define where every logical meter begins in the SM61IoT
 * register area.
 *
 * This is the main table that should be maintained when
 * meters or register assignments change.
 */
const METERS = [

    { meter_id: "B1", register: 8000 },
    { meter_id: "B2", register: 8024 },
    { meter_id: "B3", register: 8048 },
    { meter_id: "B4", register: 8072 }

];


/* =========================================================
 * Calculate meter size
 * ========================================================= */


/**
 * Calculate the number of registers occupied by one meter
 * from the configured FIELDS instead of hard-coding "24".
 *
 * Highest configured offset:
 *
 *   energy_del -> offset 22
 *
 * Float32 needs two registers:
 *
 *   22 + 2 = 24 registers
 */
const REGISTERS_PER_METER =
    Math.max(...FIELDS.map(field => field.offset)) + 2;


/* =========================================================
 * Validate configuration
 * ========================================================= */


/**
 * Check that BLOCK_SIZES describes exactly the number of
 * configured meters.
 *
 * Example:
 *
 *   METERS.length = 9
 *   BLOCK_SIZES   = [4, 5]
 *
 *   4 + 5 = 9 -> valid
 */
const configuredMeterCount =
    BLOCK_SIZES.reduce(
        (sum, blockSize) => sum + blockSize,
        0
    );


if (configuredMeterCount !== METERS.length) {

    node.error(
        "Invalid BLOCK_SIZES configuration. " +
        `BLOCK_SIZES contains ${configuredMeterCount} meters, ` +
        `but METERS contains ${METERS.length} meters.`
    );

    return null;
}


/**
 * Every block size must be a positive integer.
 */
for (const blockSize of BLOCK_SIZES) {

    if (
        !Number.isInteger(blockSize) ||
        blockSize <= 0
    ) {

        node.error(
            `Invalid block size "${blockSize}". ` +
            "Every BLOCK_SIZES entry must be a positive integer."
        );

        return null;
    }
}


/* =========================================================
 * Create common poll timestamp
 * ========================================================= */


/**
 * One timestamp is generated for the complete polling cycle.
 *
 * All Modbus requests created below belong to the same
 * measurement cycle.
 *
 * The decoder can therefore publish A1-A9 with exactly the
 * same timestamp.
 */
const pollTimestamp =
    new Date().toISOString();


/* =========================================================
 * Build Modbus requests
 * ========================================================= */


/**
 * All generated Modbus request messages are stored here.
 */
const messages = [];


/**
 * Position of the next meter that has not yet been assigned
 * to a request block.
 */
let meterIndex = 0;


/**
 * Process every configured block.
 *
 * Example:
 *
 *   BLOCK_SIZES = [4, 5]
 *
 * Iteration 1:
 *
 *   blockSize   = 4
 *   meterIndex  = 0
 *   blockMeters = A1-A4
 *
 * Iteration 2:
 *
 *   blockSize   = 5
 *   meterIndex  = 4
 *   blockMeters = A5-A9
 */
for (
    let blockIndex = 0;
    blockIndex < BLOCK_SIZES.length;
    blockIndex++
) {

    const blockSize =
        BLOCK_SIZES[blockIndex];


    /* -----------------------------------------------------
     * Select meters belonging to this block
     * ----------------------------------------------------- */

    const blockMeters =
        METERS.slice(
            meterIndex,
            meterIndex + blockSize
        );


    /*
     * This should normally never happen because BLOCK_SIZES
     * was validated above.
     */
    if (blockMeters.length === 0) {

        node.error(
            `Block ${blockIndex + 1} contains no meters.`
        );

        return null;
    }


    /* -----------------------------------------------------
     * Determine register range
     * ----------------------------------------------------- */


    /**
     * Start register is the first meter in this block.
     */
    const blockStart =
        blockMeters[0].register;


    /**
     * Determine the last meter in this block.
     */
    const lastMeter =
        blockMeters[blockMeters.length - 1];


    /**
     * Determine the register immediately AFTER the final
     * register required by the last meter.
     *
     * Example:
     *
     * A4 begins at:
     *
     *   8264
     *
     * One meter occupies:
     *
     *   24 registers
     *
     * Therefore:
     *
     *   blockEndExclusive = 8264 + 24
     *                     = 8288
     */
    const blockEndExclusive =
        lastMeter.register +
        REGISTERS_PER_METER;


    /**
     * Quantity is derived from actual start/end addresses.
     *
     * This is intentionally NOT:
     *
     *   blockMeters.length * REGISTERS_PER_METER
     *
     * Calculating from the real addresses also works if there
     * are unused/gap registers between meters.
     *
     * Example:
     *
     *   blockStart        = 8192
     *   blockEndExclusive = 8288
     *
     *   quantity          = 96
     */
    const quantity =
        blockEndExclusive -
        blockStart;


    /* -----------------------------------------------------
     * Validate Modbus FC03 quantity
     * ----------------------------------------------------- */


    if (quantity > MAX_REGISTERS_PER_REQUEST) {

        node.error(
            `Modbus block ${blockIndex + 1} is too large. ` +
            `Meters ${blockMeters[0].meter_id}-` +
            `${lastMeter.meter_id} require ${quantity} registers. ` +
            `FC03 allows a maximum of ` +
            `${MAX_REGISTERS_PER_REQUEST} registers.`
        );

        return null;
    }


    if (quantity <= 0) {

        node.error(
            `Invalid register range for block ${blockIndex + 1}.`
        );

        return null;
    }


    /* -----------------------------------------------------
     * Create Node-RED message
     * ----------------------------------------------------- */


    messages.push({

        /**
         * Same timestamp for every block in this polling cycle.
         */
        pollTimestamp: pollTimestamp,


        /**
         * Information needed later by the decoder.
         *
         * Because each request carries its own block definition,
         * the decoder does not need to know anything about
         * BLOCK_SIZES.
         *
         * It simply decodes the meters listed here.
         */
        meterConfig: {

            /**
             * Number of this request block.
             *
             * Useful for diagnostics.
             */
            blockIndex:
                blockIndex + 1,


            /**
             * Number of blocks in this polling cycle.
             */
            blockCount:
                BLOCK_SIZES.length,


            /**
             * First absolute Modbus register contained in the
             * response.
             */
            blockStartRegister:
                blockStart,


            /**
             * Number of registers expected in the response.
             */
            blockQuantity:
                quantity,


            /**
             * Size of one configured meter.
             */
            registersPerMeter:
                REGISTERS_PER_METER,


            /**
             * Float byte order used by the decoder.
             */
            floatOrder:
                FLOAT_ORDER,


            /**
             * Common field definition.
             */
            fields:
                FIELDS,


            /**
             * Only meters contained in THIS request.
             *
             * Example:
             *
             * Request 1:
             *
             *   A1, A2, A3, A4
             *
             * Request 2:
             *
             *   A5, A6, A7, A8, A9
             */
            meters:
                blockMeters

        },


        /* -------------------------------------------------
         * Actual request for Modbus Flex Getter
         * ------------------------------------------------- */

        payload: {

            /**
             * FC03 - Read Holding Registers
             */
            fc: 3,


            /**
             * Modbus TCP Unit-ID.
             */
            unitid: UNIT_ID,


            /**
             * First register to read.
             */
            address: blockStart,


            /**
             * Number of 16-bit registers to read.
             */
            quantity: quantity

        },


        /* -------------------------------------------------
         * Optional diagnostic information
         * -------------------------------------------------
         *
         * This is not required by the decoder.
         *
         * It is simply useful if you connect a Debug node
         * while commissioning the gateway.
         */
        modbusRequestInfo: {

            block:
                blockIndex + 1,

            meters:
                blockMeters.map(
                    meter => meter.meter_id
                ),

            first_register:
                blockStart,

            last_register:
                blockEndExclusive - 1,

            quantity:
                quantity

        }

    });


    /* -----------------------------------------------------
     * Advance to next group of meters
     * ----------------------------------------------------- */

    meterIndex +=
        blockSize;
}


/* =========================================================
 * Node-RED output
 * ========================================================= */


/**
 * This Function node has ONE output but creates several
 * independent messages.
 *
 * With:
 *
 *   BLOCK_SIZES = [4, 5]
 *
 * Node-RED sends:
 *
 *   Message 1:
 *       A1-A4
 *       Address 8192
 *       Quantity 96
 *
 *   Message 2:
 *       A5-A9
 *       Address 8288
 *       Quantity 120
 *
 *
 * With:
 *
 *   BLOCK_SIZES = [3, 3, 3]
 *
 * Node-RED sends:
 *
 *   Message 1 -> A1-A3
 *   Message 2 -> A4-A6
 *   Message 3 -> A7-A9
 *
 *
 * The messages are sent sequentially into output 1.
 */
return [messages];

     * Quantity is derived from actual start/end addresses.
     *
     * This is intentionally NOT:
     *
     *   blockMeters.length * REGISTERS_PER_METER
     *

     * are unused/gap registers between meters.
     *
     * Example:
     *
     *   blockStart        = 8192
     *   blockEndExclusive = 8288
     *
     *   quantity          = 96

    const quantity =
        blockEndExclusive -
        blockStart;


    /* -----------------------------------------------------
     * Validate Modbus FC03 quantity
     * ----------------------------------------------------- */


    if (quantity > MAX_REGISTERS_PER_REQUEST) {

        node.error(
            `Modbus block ${blockIndex + 1} is too large. ` +
            `Meters ${blockMeters[0].meter_id}-` +
            `${lastMeter.meter_id} require ${quantity} registers. ` +
            `FC03 allows a maximum of ` +
            `${MAX_REGISTERS_PER_REQUEST} registers.`
        );

        return null;
    }


    if (quantity <= 0) {

        node.error(
            `Invalid register range for block ${blockIndex + 1}.`
        );

        return null;
    }


    /* -----------------------------------------------------
     * Create Node-RED message
     * ----------------------------------------------------- */


    messages.push({

        /**
         * Same timestamp for every block in this polling cycle.
         */
        pollTimestamp: pollTimestamp,


        /**
         * Information needed later by the decoder.
         *
         * Because each request carries its own block definition,
         * the decoder does not need to know anything about
         * BLOCK_SIZES.
         *
         * It simply decodes the meters listed here.
         */
        meterConfig: {

            /**
             * Number of this request block.
             *
             * Useful for diagnostics.
             */

             * First absolute Modbus register contained in the

            /**
             * Number of registers expected in the response.
             */

                quantity,


            /**
             * Size of one configured meter.
             */
            registersPerMeter:
                REGISTERS_PER_METER,


            /**
             * Float byte order used by the decoder.
             */
            floatOrder:
                FLOAT_ORDER,


            /**
             * Common field definition.
             */
            fields:
                FIELDS,


            /**
             * Only meters contained in THIS request.
             *
             * Example:
             *
             * Request 1:
             *
             *   A1, A2, A3, A4
             *

             *   A5, A6, A7, A8, A9
             */
            meters:
                blockMeters

        },


        /* -------------------------------------------------
         * Actual request for Modbus Flex Getter
         * ------------------------------------------------- */

        payload: {

            /**
             * FC03 - Read Holding Registers
             */
            fc: 3,


            /**
             * Modbus TCP Unit-ID.
             */
            unitid: UNIT_ID,


            /**
             * First register to read.
             */
            address: blockStart,


            /**
             * Number of 16-bit registers to read.
             */
            quantity: quantity

        },


        /* -------------------------------------------------
         * Optional diagnostic information
         * -------------------------------------------------
         *
         * This is not required by the decoder.
         *
         * It is simply useful if you connect a Debug node
         * while commissioning the gateway.
         */
        modbusRequestInfo: {

            block:
                blockIndex + 1,

            meters:
                blockMeters.map(
                    meter => meter.meter_id
                ),

            first_register:
                blockStart,

            last_register:
                blockEndExclusive - 1,

            quantity:
                quantity

    });


    /* -----------------------------------------------------
     * Advance to next group of meters
     * ----------------------------------------------------- */

    meterIndex +=
        blockSize;

 * Node-RED output
 * ========================================================= */


/**
 * This Function node has ONE output but creates several
 * independent messages.
 *
 * With:
 *
 *   BLOCK_SIZES = [4, 5]

 *   Message 1:

 */

func:
/**
 * Build Modbus requests for all configured electricity meters.
 *
 * PURPOSE
 * -------
 * The SM61IoT exposes the meter values as consecutive Modbus registers.
 *
 * Each electricity meter contains:
 *
 *   12 Float32 values
 *   2 Modbus registers per Float32 value
 *
 * Therefore one meter normally occupies:
 *
 *   12 * 2 = 24 Modbus registers
 *
 *
 * WHY MULTIPLE REQUESTS?
 * ----------------------
 * Modbus FC03 allows a maximum of 125 registers per request.
 *
 * Therefore multiple meters may need to be split into several requests.
 *
 * The split is configured explicitly using BLOCK_SIZES.
 *
 *
 * EXAMPLES
 * --------
 *
 * 9 meters split as 4 + 5:
 *
 *   const BLOCK_SIZES = [4, 5];
 *
 * Results in:
 *
 *   Request 1 -> A1-A4
 *   Request 2 -> A5-A9
 *
 *
 * 9 meters split as 3 + 3 + 3:
 *
 *   const BLOCK_SIZES = [3, 3, 3];
 *
 *
 * 8 meters split as 3 + 5:
 *
 *   const BLOCK_SIZES = [3, 5];
 *
 *
 * 7 meters split as 3 + 4:
 *
 *   const BLOCK_SIZES = [3, 4];
 *
 *
 * IMPORTANT
 * ---------
 * The sum of BLOCK_SIZES must exactly match the number of meters
 * configured in METERS.
 */


/* =========================================================
 * Modbus configuration
 * ========================================================= */


/**
 * Modbus TCP Unit-ID / Slave-ID of the SM61IoT.
 */
const UNIT_ID = 255;


/**
 * Float byte order used by the meter values.
 *
 * The currently observed values indicate ABCD.
 */
const FLOAT_ORDER = "ABCD";


/**
 * Maximum number of registers allowed by FC03.
 *
 * According to the Modbus specification:
 *
 *   FC03 quantity = 1 ... 125 registers
 */
const MAX_REGISTERS_PER_REQUEST = 125;


/* =========================================================
 * Request block configuration
 * ========================================================= */


/**
 * Define how many meters should be read in each Modbus request.
 *
 * Current gateway:
 *
 *   9 meters
 *
 * Split:
 *
 *   Request 1 -> 4 meters
 *   Request 2 -> 5 meters
 *
 * Therefore:
 */
const BLOCK_SIZES = [4, 4];


/*
 * Other valid examples:
 *
 * const BLOCK_SIZES = [3, 3, 3];
 *
 * const BLOCK_SIZES = [3, 4];
 *
 * const BLOCK_SIZES = [3, 5];
 *
 * const BLOCK_SIZES = [2, 2, 2, 3];
 */


/* =========================================================
 * Meter field layout
 * ========================================================= */


/**
 * Every field is one Float32 value.
 *
 * One Float32 occupies two consecutive 16-bit Modbus registers.
 *
 * The offset is relative to the first register of the meter.
 */
const FIELDS = [

    { name: "u_l1_n",     offset: 0  },
    { name: "u_l2_n",     offset: 2  },
    { name: "u_l3_n",     offset: 4  },

    { name: "i_l1",       offset: 6  },
    { name: "i_l2",       offset: 8  },
    { name: "i_l3",       offset: 10 },

    { name: "p_l1",       offset: 12 },
    { name: "p_l2",       offset: 14 },
    { name: "p_l3",       offset: 16 },

    { name: "p_sum",      offset: 18 },

    { name: "energy_con", offset: 20 },
    { name: "energy_del", offset: 22 }

];


/* =========================================================
 * Meter / register relationship
 * ========================================================= */


/**
 * Define where every logical meter begins in the SM61IoT
 * register area.
 *
 * This is the main table that should be maintained when
 * meters or register assignments change.
 */
const METERS = [

    { meter_id: "A1", register: 8000 },
    { meter_id: "A2", register: 8024 },
    { meter_id: "A3", register: 8048 },
    { meter_id: "A4", register: 8072 },

    { meter_id: "A5", register: 8096 },
    { meter_id: "A6", register: 8120 },
    { meter_id: "A7", register: 8144 },
    { meter_id: "A8", register: 8168 }

];


/* =========================================================
 * Calculate meter size
 * ========================================================= */


/**
 * Calculate the number of registers occupied by one meter
 * from the configured FIELDS instead of hard-coding "24".
 *
 * Highest configured offset:
 *
 *   energy_del -> offset 22
 *
 * Float32 needs two registers:
 *
 *   22 + 2 = 24 registers
 */
const REGISTERS_PER_METER =
    Math.max(...FIELDS.map(field => field.offset)) + 2;


/* =========================================================
 * Validate configuration
 * ========================================================= */


/**
 * Check that BLOCK_SIZES describes exactly the number of
 * configured meters.
 *
 * Example:
 *
 *   METERS.length = 9
 *   BLOCK_SIZES   = [4, 5]
 *
 *   4 + 5 = 9 -> valid
 */
const configuredMeterCount =
    BLOCK_SIZES.reduce(
        (sum, blockSize) => sum + blockSize,
        0
    );


if (configuredMeterCount !== METERS.length) {

    node.error(
        "Invalid BLOCK_SIZES configuration. " +
        `BLOCK_SIZES contains ${configuredMeterCount} meters, ` +
        `but METERS contains ${METERS.length} meters.`
    );

    return null;
}


/**
 * Every block size must be a positive integer.
 */
for (const blockSize of BLOCK_SIZES) {

    if (
        !Number.isInteger(blockSize) ||
        blockSize <= 0
    ) {

        node.error(
            `Invalid block size "${blockSize}". ` +
            "Every BLOCK_SIZES entry must be a positive integer."
        );

        return null;
    }
}


/* =========================================================
 * Create common poll timestamp
 * ========================================================= */


/**
 * One timestamp is generated for the complete polling cycle.
 *
 * All Modbus requests created below belong to the same
 * measurement cycle.
 *
 * The decoder can therefore publish A1-A9 with exactly the
 * same timestamp.
 */
const pollTimestamp =
    new Date().toISOString();


/* =========================================================
 * Build Modbus requests
 * ========================================================= */


/**
 * All generated Modbus request messages are stored here.
 */
const messages = [];


/**
 * Position of the next meter that has not yet been assigned
 * to a request block.
 */
let meterIndex = 0;


/**
 * Process every configured block.
 *
 * Example:
 *
 *   BLOCK_SIZES = [4, 5]
 *
 * Iteration 1:
 *
 *   blockSize   = 4
 *   meterIndex  = 0
 *   blockMeters = A1-A4
 *
 * Iteration 2:
 *
 *   blockSize   = 5
 *   meterIndex  = 4
 *   blockMeters = A5-A9
 */
for (
    let blockIndex = 0;
    blockIndex < BLOCK_SIZES.length;
    blockIndex++
) {

    const blockSize =
        BLOCK_SIZES[blockIndex];


    /* -----------------------------------------------------
     * Select meters belonging to this block
     * ----------------------------------------------------- */

    const blockMeters =
        METERS.slice(
            meterIndex,
            meterIndex + blockSize
        );


    /*
     * This should normally never happen because BLOCK_SIZES
     * was validated above.
     */
    if (blockMeters.length === 0) {

        node.error(
            `Block ${blockIndex + 1} contains no meters.`
        );

        return null;
    }


    /* -----------------------------------------------------
     * Determine register range
     * ----------------------------------------------------- */


    /**
     * Start register is the first meter in this block.
     */
    const blockStart =
        blockMeters[0].register;


    /**
     * Determine the last meter in this block.
     */
    const lastMeter =
        blockMeters[blockMeters.length - 1];


    /**
     * Determine the register immediately AFTER the final
     * register required by the last meter.
     *
     * Example:
     *
     * A4 begins at:
     *
     *   8264
     *
     * One meter occupies:
     *
     *   24 registers
     *
     * Therefore:
     *
     *   blockEndExclusive = 8264 + 24
     *                     = 8288
     */
    const blockEndExclusive =
        lastMeter.register +
        REGISTERS_PER_METER;


    /**
     * Quantity is derived from actual start/end addresses.
     *
     * This is intentionally NOT:
     *
     *   blockMeters.length * REGISTERS_PER_METER
     *
     * Calculating from the real addresses also works if there
     * are unused/gap registers between meters.
     *
     * Example:
     *
     *   blockStart        = 8192
     *   blockEndExclusive = 8288
     *
     *   quantity          = 96
     */
    const quantity =
        blockEndExclusive -
        blockStart;


    /* -----------------------------------------------------
     * Validate Modbus FC03 quantity
     * ----------------------------------------------------- */


    if (quantity > MAX_REGISTERS_PER_REQUEST) {

        node.error(
            `Modbus block ${blockIndex + 1} is too large. ` +
            `Meters ${blockMeters[0].meter_id}-` +
            `${lastMeter.meter_id} require ${quantity} registers. ` +
            `FC03 allows a maximum of ` +
            `${MAX_REGISTERS_PER_REQUEST} registers.`
        );

        return null;
    }


    if (quantity <= 0) {

        node.error(
            `Invalid register range for block ${blockIndex + 1}.`
        );

        return null;
    }


    /* -----------------------------------------------------
     * Create Node-RED message
     * ----------------------------------------------------- */


    messages.push({

        /**
         * Same timestamp for every block in this polling cycle.
         */
        pollTimestamp: pollTimestamp,


        /**
         * Information needed later by the decoder.
         *
         * Because each request carries its own block definition,
         * the decoder does not need to know anything about
         * BLOCK_SIZES.
         *
         * It simply decodes the meters listed here.
         */
        meterConfig: {

            /**
             * Number of this request block.
             *
             * Useful for diagnostics.
             */
            blockIndex:
                blockIndex + 1,


            /**
             * Number of blocks in this polling cycle.
             */
            blockCount:
                BLOCK_SIZES.length,


            /**
             * First absolute Modbus register contained in the
             * response.
             */
            blockStartRegister:
                blockStart,


            /**
             * Number of registers expected in the response.
             */
            blockQuantity:
                quantity,


            /**
             * Size of one configured meter.
             */
            registersPerMeter:
                REGISTERS_PER_METER,


            /**
             * Float byte order used by the decoder.
             */
            floatOrder:
                FLOAT_ORDER,


            /**
             * Common field definition.
             */
            fields:
                FIELDS,


            /**
             * Only meters contained in THIS request.
             *
             * Example:
             *
             * Request 1:
             *
             *   A1, A2, A3, A4
             *
             * Request 2:
             *
             *   A5, A6, A7, A8, A9
             */
            meters:
                blockMeters

        },


        /* -------------------------------------------------
         * Actual request for Modbus Flex Getter
         * ------------------------------------------------- */

        payload: {

            /**
             * FC03 - Read Holding Registers
             */
            fc: 3,


            /**
             * Modbus TCP Unit-ID.
             */
            unitid: UNIT_ID,


            /**
             * First register to read.
             */
            address: blockStart,


            /**
             * Number of 16-bit registers to read.
             */
            quantity: quantity

        },


        /* -------------------------------------------------
         * Optional diagnostic information
         * -------------------------------------------------
         *
         * This is not required by the decoder.
         *
         * It is simply useful if you connect a Debug node
         * while commissioning the gateway.
         */
        modbusRequestInfo: {

            block:
                blockIndex + 1,

            meters:
                blockMeters.map(
                    meter => meter.meter_id
                ),

            first_register:
                blockStart,

            last_register:
                blockEndExclusive - 1,

            quantity:
                quantity

        }

    });


    /* -----------------------------------------------------
     * Advance to next group of meters
     * ----------------------------------------------------- */

    meterIndex +=
        blockSize;
}


/* =========================================================
 * Node-RED output
 * ========================================================= */


/**
 * This Function node has ONE output but creates several
 * independent messages.
 *
 * With:
 *
 *   BLOCK_SIZES = [4, 5]
 *
 * Node-RED sends:
 *
 *   Message 1:
 *       A1-A4
 *       Address 8192
 *       Quantity 96
 *
 *   Message 2:
 *       A5-A9
 *       Address 8288
 *       Quantity 120
 *
 *
 * With:
 *
 *   BLOCK_SIZES = [3, 3, 3]
 *
 * Node-RED sends:
 *
 *   Message 1 -> A1-A3
 *   Message 2 -> A4-A6
 *   Message 3 -> A7-A9

 * The messages are sent sequentially into output 1.

name: Connect
func:
/**
 * Force a fresh Modbus TCP connection before each polling cycle.
 *
 * WHY?
 * ----
 * The SM61IoT closes idle Modbus TCP connections after its configured
 * "Port closing time". With a polling interval of 60 seconds, the socket
 * may already have been closed by the gateway when the next poll starts.
 *
 * node-red-contrib-modbus can still think the old socket exists until it
 * tries to use it, resulting in:
 *
 *   "Modbus client socket not readable"
 *
 * Therefore we explicitly reconnect before performing the actual
 * Modbus read.
 *
 * IMPORTANT:
 * The Modbus Flex Connector and the Modbus Flex Getter must use the
 * SAME "Modbus Client" configuration node.
 */


/* SM61IoT network configuration */
const MODBUS_HOST = "10.40.22.114";
const MODBUS_PORT = 502;
const UNIT_ID = 255;


/**
 * Modbus Flex Connector expects its configuration in msg.payload.
 *
 * connectorType = TCP
 * tcpType       = DEFAULT because the SM61IoT provides native Modbus TCP.
 */
msg.payload = {

    connectorType: "TCP",

    tcpHost: MODBUS_HOST,

    tcpPort: MODBUS_PORT,

    tcpType: "DEFAULT",

    unitId: UNIT_ID,

    /**
     * How long to wait for an individual Modbus transaction.
     */
    clientTimeout: 3000,

    /**
     * Delay used by the client between commands.
     */
    commandDelay: 100,

    /**
     * Delay used for automatic reconnect attempts.
     */
    reconnectTimeout: 2000
};


/**
 * Remember when this poll cycle started.
 *
 * The timestamp can later be passed through the Modbus request
 * and used for all meter MQTT messages belonging to this cycle.
 */
msg.pollTimestamp = new Date().toISOString();


return msg;

info:
# Insert Queue

Process of this subflow:
 1. queue messages
 2. insert message by message into postgresql node
 3. drop the message from the queue, when it was processed succesfull
 4. peek a new message from the queue
 5. repeat

Each input will be queued inside the q-gate node. (FIFO)
During start of the subflow a Trigger will be activated. This trigger will send a "control: peek" message at a given interval.
This is necessary because when the queue is empty we need to periodically check if a new message is available.
When a message is dequeued the trigger will be deactivated (msg.reset: true) until the message is processed by the postgresql node.
